撰写论文 Conclusion 章节（\section{Conclusion}），输出完整 LaTeX 到本地文件：

### Para 1: Summary
- 本文是首个系统性 per-example 分析，研究 attention 在 hybrid recurrent architectures 中的均衡效应

- 基于 aggregate benchmarks 的架构选择可能掩盖 per-example behavioral differences
- 这些差异对部署可靠性和 ensemble 构建有实际影响
- 连接到 underspecification (D'Amour et al. 2022) — 我们量化了这一现象在 hybrid architectures 中的具体表现

- Interventional experiments (attention head ablation/swaps) — 从 observational 到 causal

- Other hybrid families (Jamba, RWKV-6) — generalization

\section{Conclusion}

This paper presents the first systematic per-example analysis of how attention affects cross-architecture agreement in hybrid recurrent models. Using the controlled model zoo of \citet{wang2025hybrid}, we compared three recurrent architectures across five attention ratios and two parameter scales. The central result is that aggregate performance convergence and per-example behavioral divergence are decoupled: these two quantities follow different trajectories as attention increases.

Three findings support this conclusion. First, attention-driven convergence is task-specific: among ten benchmarks, only LAMBADA, a pure context-retrieval task, shows monotonic reduction in cross-architecture variance. Reasoning and comprehension benchmarks show no such pattern. Second, convergence depends on scale. The 1.3B models exhibit complete monotonic convergence on LAMBADA, while the 340M models follow a non-monotonic trajectory with only partial variance reduction. Third, aggregate convergence and per-example divergence operate on different timescales. Cross-architecture variance on LAMBADA decreases gradually across attention ratios, but pairwise overlap between architectures' per-example effect sets saturates at the lowest attention level and does not increase further. The architectures reach similar overall scores through different per-example trade-offs.

These results carry a practical consequence for architecture selection. Choosing between recurrent backbones on the basis of aggregate benchmark scores can obscure per-example behavioral differences that persist after aggregate metrics converge. For deployment scenarios where per-input reliability matters, or for ensemble construction where member diversity determines error reduction, aggregate equivalence does not imply behavioral interchangeability. This observation connects to the underspecification framework of \citet{damour2022underspecification}: we quantify how architectural variation in hybrid recurrent models produces the same type of per-prediction divergence that prior work attributed to random initialization and training noise.

Several directions remain open. Interventional experiments, such as attention head ablation or cross-architecture head transplantation, could establish causal rather than observational links between attention and per-example effects. Additional scale points beyond 1.3B would clarify whether the convergence pattern extends or saturates at larger capacity. Testing other hybrid families such as Jamba and RWKV-6 would probe the generality of the decoupling across recurrent designs. Our analysis covers pretrained models only; fine-tuning may alter the dynamics reported here.

\section*{Limitations}

Our analysis has several limitations that constrain the scope of its conclusions.

\paragraph{Statistical power.} With only $n = 5$ attention ratios, the minimum achievable two-tailed $p$-value under an exact permutation test is approximately 0.008. This ceiling limits our ability to detect weak convergence effects and contributes to the Bonferroni-adjusted $p = .100$ for LAMBADA not reaching conventional significance. We report confidence intervals as primary evidence to partially address this constraint.

\paragraph{Per-example scope.} Our per-example decomposition is limited to LAMBADA, the only benchmark with statistically supported convergence. Extending helped/hurt analysis to benchmarks without convergence would not test the central claim, but examining per-example effects on tasks with moderate but non-significant convergence (e.g., ARC-Easy, MMLU) could reveal whether the decoupling pattern generalizes.

\paragraph{Scale coverage.} We compare two scale points (340M and 1.3B parameters). The contrast between complete convergence at 1.3B and partial convergence at 340M is a binary observation, not a scaling law. Intermediate and larger scales would be needed to characterize the functional relationship between model capacity and convergence.

\paragraph{Architecture coverage.} Our study examines three recurrent architectures (GatedDeltaNet, RetNet, HGRN2) from one model zoo. Other hybrid families, including Jamba, RWKV-6, and Hymba, use different mixing strategies that may produce different per-example patterns. Generalization beyond these three architectures requires additional controlled experiments.

\paragraph{Observational design.} Our attention weight analysis is descriptive, not causal. We report cosine similarities and entropy differences between helped and hurt examples but cannot determine whether attention patterns cause the per-example effects or merely correlate with them. Interventional methods such as attention head ablation would be necessary to establish causal links.

\paragraph{Pre-training only.} All models in our study are evaluated after pre-training without fine-tuning. Per-example effects may change under task-specific adaptation, and the decoupling pattern we observe may not persist after fine-tuning.

\section{Conclusion}

This paper presents the first systematic per-example analysis of how attention affects cross-architecture agreement in hybrid recurrent models. Using the controlled model zoo of \citet{wang2025hybrid}, we compared three recurrent architectures across five attention ratios and two parameter scales. The central result is that aggregate performance convergence and per-example behavioral divergence are decoupled: these two quantities follow different trajectories as attention increases.

Three findings support this conclusion. First, attention-driven convergence is task-specific: among ten benchmarks, only LAMBADA, a pure context-retrieval task, shows monotonic reduction in cross-architecture variance. Reasoning and comprehension benchmarks show no such pattern. Second, convergence depends on scale. The 1.3B models exhibit complete monotonic convergence on LAMBADA, while the 340M models follow a non-monotonic trajectory with only partial variance reduction. Third, aggregate convergence and per-example divergence operate on different timescales. Cross-architecture variance on LAMBADA decreases gradually across attention ratios, but pairwise overlap between architectures' per-example effect sets saturates at the lowest attention level and does not increase further. The architectures reach similar overall scores through different per-example trade-offs.

These results carry a practical consequence for architecture selection. Choosing between recurrent backbones on the basis of aggregate benchmark scores can obscure per-example behavioral differences that persist after aggregate metrics converge. For deployment scenarios where per-input reliability matters, or for ensemble construction where member diversity determines error reduction, aggregate equivalence does not imply behavioral interchangeability. This observation connects to the underspecification framework of \citet{damour2022underspecification}: we quantify how architectural variation in hybrid recurrent models produces the same type of per-prediction divergence that prior work attributed to random initialization and training noise.

Several directions remain open. Interventional experiments, such as attention head ablation or cross-architecture head transplantation, could establish causal rather than observational links between attention and per-example effects. Additional scale points beyond 1.3B would clarify whether the convergence pattern extends or saturates at larger capacity. Testing other hybrid families such as Jamba and RWKV-6 would probe the generality of the decoupling across recurrent designs. Our analysis covers pretrained models only; fine-tuning may alter the dynamics reported here.
